**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: one and three quarter hours.**

Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the market price for cocoa and why?

(i) Before the application of fertilizer? (3 marks)

(ii) After the application of fertilizer? (3 marks)
List four other factors apart from the application of fertilizer that can cause the supply of cocoa to increase. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Supply increases (the supply curve shifts to the right) when producers are willing and able to offer more at every price. Four factors other than fertilizer:

1. **A fall in the cost of production**: cheaper inputs such as labour, pesticides, sacks or transport, so that each ton is more profitable to supply.
2. **Improved technology and farming methods**: high-yielding or disease-resistant cocoa varieties, better spraying and drying techniques.
3. **Favourable weather conditions** and the absence of pests and diseases (good rainfall, no black pod disease), which raise the harvest.
4. **Government subsidies or lower taxes** on cocoa farmers (for example free or cheap seedlings, reduced export duties).

Other acceptable factors: an increase in the number of cocoa farms or farmers (new plantations coming into production), a fall in the price of competing crops that use the same land (coffee, banana, so that farmers switch to cocoa), better rural roads and storage facilities, and cheaper credit.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Suppose farmers, through their cooperative union, decide to operate a buffer stock scheme in order to stabilize the price of cocoa as in a (i) above.

(i) Briefly explain how such a scheme functions to stabilize prices. (3 marks)

(ii) How many tons of cocoa must the union buy after the application of fertilizer as in (a i) above? (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) How a buffer stock scheme works.** The union (or a marketing board) fixes a target price, here 60 000 FCFA per ton, usually with a small band around it (a minimum and a maximum price).

- When the harvest is large and supply is greater than demand, the market price tends to fall below the minimum price. The union **buys the surplus** with its funds and **stores it** (the "buffer stock"). This extra demand keeps the price up at the target.
- When the harvest is poor and demand is greater than supply, the market price tends to rise above the maximum price. The union **sells from its stock**, which adds to supply and pulls the price back down to the target.

Buying in good years and selling in bad years keeps the price close to the target, which stabilizes the incomes of farmers and protects consumers from price spikes.

**(ii) Tons to be bought.** The price to be maintained is the price of part (a)(i), 60 thousand FCFA per ton. After the use of fertilizer, at that price:

- quantity supplied = 480 tons;
- quantity demanded = 240 tons.

The union must buy the excess supply to prevent the price from falling towards 40:

$$480 - 240 = 240 \text{ tons}$$

**The union must buy 240 tons.** (At the target price this costs $240 \times 60\,000 = 14\,400\,000$ FCFA, which shows how much money the scheme needs.)

questions.enonce_markdown: State two reasons why the price of cocoa is likely to fluctuate if it is not controlled. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Unstable supply.** Cocoa output depends on the weather, pests and diseases, and farmers cannot adjust output quickly because cocoa trees take years to bear fruit. A good or bad harvest therefore moves supply sharply from year to year.
2. **Inelastic demand and supply in the short run, and changes in world demand.** Both demand and supply of an agricultural product respond little to price in the short run, so a small shift in supply or in world demand (a change in consumers' incomes abroad, a change in exchange rates, speculation on commodity markets) causes a large change in the price.

questions.enonce_markdown: List two limitations to the scheme mentioned in (c) above. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Costly to run.** The union needs a large fund to buy the surplus, and it must pay for storage, handling and insurance. Cocoa can deteriorate in store, so stocks cannot be kept for ever.
2. **Difficulty in fixing the right price.** If the target price is set too high, farmers over-produce and stocks pile up that cannot be sold; if it is set too low, the union runs out of stock in a bad year and cannot defend the price.

Other acceptable limitations: poor management or corruption in the union, and the fact that the scheme may encourage inefficient farmers to stay in production.
